openings.claim: Locator instability dominates retrieval delay: household surnames and stale exceptions send the clerk to the wrong first location. Fast cart pickups in O4 remain awkward but compatible with fresh arrivals having recognizable, current locations.
openings.delta: Replace the assumption that shelving accelerates retrieval with a distinction between truthful and misleading location cues.
openings.prediction: Within comparable search-set sizes and rush conditions, long searches concentrate on inaccurate cues; accurate shelf searches approach accurate cart searches.
openings.rival_prediction: Physical search interference dominates instead: even accurate shelf cues leave retrieval slower than comparably sized cart searches.
openings.defeat: Accurately cued shelf pickups consistently remain slower than matched cart pickups, with few delays attributable to inaccurate cues.
openings.probe: Use the existing timing sheet for a bounded sample of routine pickups: record first cue, actual location, candidate-set size, rush status and retrieval time behind the desk. Retain ordinary identity verification. Include all added preparation and correction work within ten clerk-minutes; stop annotation at the cap. Compare accurate shelf/cart cases and inaccurate/accurate cases.
assumptions: Evaluating a capped observational probe, not a proven intervention or attainment of 95% within two minutes.
Comparable shelf/cart cases may not occur; without them the probe is inconclusive.

openings.claim: Physical search interference dominates: crowded shelf arrangements impede recognition, whereas cart presentation permits rapid identification. O4 directly challenges shelving superiority; O2/O3 can compound delays without being their main cause.
openings.delta: Treat storage presentation as a retrieval variable independent of locator correctness.
openings.prediction: In the same probe, accurate shelf pickups remain slower than accurate cart pickups with comparable candidate counts and rush conditions.
openings.rival_prediction: Locator instability predicts little shelf/cart difference once cues are accurate, with delays concentrated on mismatches.
openings.defeat: Matched accurate shelf/cart retrieval times converge while inaccurate cues account for the long searches.
openings.probe: Use exactly the A1 probe and its stopping rule; the discriminating observation is a persistent shelf/cart time gap among accurately cued, comparable pickups.
assumptions: Cart visibility is hypothesized, not supplied evidence.
Book size and arrival recency may confound comparisons.
No benefit or target attainment is established.
